trust_decision.summary: Only an actor who passes canEditAuthFields (and editableOnDemo) for a target user may change that user's activated / ldap_import flags, decided per-target-user inside BulkUsersController; bulk merge additionally requires users.delete.

landing_point.why: The summary names ldap_import and activated as bulk-editable; that is exactly where both fields are added to the shared mass-update array, twelve lines above the single UPDATE that writes them for every selected user.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /users/bulkedit (route users/bulkedit, BulkUsersController@edit, renders the form)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The REST update already strips username, email, activated, password and permissions out of fill() and gates them one by one, so ldap_import reads as an ordinary profile field; and the advisory is written about the bulk-edit screen, not the API.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Bulk edits of the non-auth fields (city, display_name, location_id, start_date, autoassign_licenses) must keep applying to admin/superuser targets for an actor who may not edit auth fields, and groups[] sync must keep running for every user the actor may edit. The published fix only pulls activated/ldap_import out of the mass update and leaves the rest in User::whereIn()->update(), so a fix that instead skips protected targets for the whole update_array silently stops city/display_name/location edits on admins.

O6_input_shapes: activated / ldap_import sent as the radio value '0' (PHP-falsy but Laravel-filled), i.e. deactivate / allow-password-management must still be applied, not treated as 'do not change'
ids[] array mixing admin or superuser targets with ordinary users in one submission (per-user decision required inside one request)
groups[] present or absent in the same request as the auth fields, sharing the new per-user loop

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PATCH/PUT /api/v1/users/{id} writes ldap_import straight through $user->fill($request->except([...])) - ldap_import is missing from the except list - so an actor with users.edit but no canEditAuthFields can set ldap_import on a superuser
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The neighbouring lines already exclude activated and the other sensitive fields and gate them at :544, so ldap_import looks like an ordinary field this route is meant to accept; the advisory talks about the bulk-edit form.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another controller in app/Http/Controllers/Api, ~370 lines below the landing point, different transport (Passport-token REST)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PUT/PATCH /users/{id} (single-user edit) assigns activated from the request at :295, before the canEditAuthFields block at :303, so the submitted value survives when the actor may not edit auth fields and the admin/superuser can be deactivated
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The edit blade disables the activated radios with @cannot('canEditAuthFields', $user), so the UI cannot submit the field and the remainder of the method looks gated.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling controller in the same namespace, ~240 lines above the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second bulk controller using the identical conditionallyAddItem / $update_array / whereIn()->update() mass-update idiom
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pattern was copied across Snipe-IT's bulk controllers (BulkAssetsController and this one share the same private helper), so a maintainer adding a permission-sensitive model column here is entirely plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CSV user import carries its own hand-rolled auth-field guard that unsets username/email/password/activated but not ldap_import
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same 'auth fields on a user you may not edit' rule implemented a second time without a shared helper, so extending it to ldap_import in a later change is exactly how this class of bug recurs.

O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization - broken access control via mass assignment of privileged user flags (activated / ldap_import)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP ^8.2 with ext-curl/fileinfo/iconv/json/mbstring/pdo, Composer (Laravel 12, PHPUnit 10.5 per phpunit.xml); npm/Vite only for UI assets, not needed for feature tests
services: none required for tests: .env.unit-tests sets DB_CONNECTION=sqlite_testing (in-memory sqlite, config/database.php:78-82); production .env.example uses MySQL/MariaDB
O10_build.project_tests: PHPUnit feature tests under tests/Feature/Users (e.g. tests/Feature/Users/Ui/BulkActions/BulkDeleteUsersTest.php, tests/Feature/Users/Ui/MergeUsersTest.php, tests/Feature/Users/Api/UpdateUserTest.php); the suite aborts unless a .env.testing file exists (tests/TestCase.php:51-58), which the repo only ships as examples/.env.unit-tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep the existing single mass update but wrap it in the canEditAuthFields condition (or filter $user_raw_array down to editable users), which fixes the reported fields and silently stops city/display_name/location bulk edits on admin targets and can drop the groups sync.

out_of_scope_notes: app/Console/Commands/LdapSync.php and app/Models/Ldap.php write activated/ldap_import without any canEditAuthFields gate, but they are CLI/sync machinery outside this advisory's HTTP surface and were not pursued.
